Tang Dynasty. One of the main architectural attractions is the Great White Pagoda which is popularly also known as Qianfo Temple. The pagoda was built sometime during the Northern Wei Dynasty (386-534AD) and actually used to be located in the palace of the regional king. During the Tang Dynasty (618-906AD) the temple was expanded and renamed to its current name of Qianfosi.

While the temple was founded during the Tang Dynasty it was greatly expanded during the Song and Ming Dynasties, which is why the temple sits just one meter below ground level. Currently the temple grounds occupy around 65,000 square meters and are home to over 400 halls and rooms that include thirteen pagodas. The highlight and namesake of the temple is the Great White Pagoda which rests on over thirteen thousand wood piles. The pagoda rises to a height of fifty- nine meters and is composed of ten levels. Interestingly, during the Qing Dynasty the northern part of the temple was abandoned and now serves as the Meridian Municipal Museum
